status: Frozen on owner approval (October 2, 2026). The owner accepted the draft defaults and chose to run on the owner's workstation, where records.json and the calendar are available. No SEC request, exhibit read or 10-Q value projection has been made; probe.py makes the requests only when the owner runs it.
question: For a seeded random sample of strategy-qualified 10-Q events whose only Item 2.02 8-K maps to an earlier decision session, does that 8-K's original press-release exhibit state the same S and Q input values, for the same periods, that the later 10-Q reports?
why: Both metadata audits found an earlier Item 2.02 8-K for most 10-Qs (disclosure-timing20261001: 63.9-64.4% of qualified events by decision session; disclosure-novelty20261001: 2,484 of 4,057 originals by ET date). Timing does not show content. Only a component shown to be stated in the earlier release may ever move to the earlier clock.

S.definition: (current-quarter net income - prior-year same-quarter net income) / prior fiscal-year-end total assets, standardized by the issuer's previous eight innovations (unchanged)

Q.definition: ((current YTD operating cash flow - current YTD net income) - (prior-year YTD operating cash flow - prior-year YTD net income)) / prior fiscal-year-end total assets

components.note: The S history of eight earlier innovations was already public through earlier 10-Qs and is not probed.

release_sets.reason: Prior fiscal-year-end total assets were normally public earlier through the prior annual report, like the eight historical S innovations. The verdict therefore uses the flow components; assets are reported separately as stated or not stated in the release. A later full extraction must bind assets to the earlier annual filing's verified clock and value; this probe does not fetch annual reports.

population.rule: strategy_source_qualified is true and status is single_prior
population.excluded: multiple (which release applies is ambiguous), single_same_session (no earlier session), single_after, no_candidate and window_coverage_incomplete

sample.order: ascending SHA256 of the UTF-8 string 'exhibit-content20261002|' + 10-Q accession number; take the first 150
sample.replacement: none: a failed fetch, missing exhibit, identity failure or unmatched value stays in the sample and its denominator

requests.archive: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/{issuer CIK as an integer, no leading zeros}/{8-K accession without dashes}/ — the frozen capture's archive_base rule, keyed by the issuer CIK. 402 of the 1,166 frame 8-Ks were filed by an agent whose CIK is the accession prefix, so the prefix must never be used.
per_event: every document whose index type starts with EX-99, in index order, at most 10; an index with more than 10 fetches none of them and the event is exhibit_overflow
requests.redirects: none; a redirect is saved as a failure
requests.user_agent: FrontierResearch/0.1 (bounded local SEC source-feasibility study; no contact address configured)
never: images, XBRL or any non-EX-99 document
prices, returns, forecasts or account ledgers
requests.caps_basis: max_lifetime_network_attempts 1,800 = 150 events x (index + header + up to 10 EX-99 documents); max_attempts_per_url 2 allows one retry of an interrupted request

storage: Every response's exact bytes under source/raw/<sha256>.bin, referenced from the request journal, following the frozen capture convention.

rules: header filer CIK equals the issuer CIK
header item information includes Results of Operations and Financial Condition (Item 2.02) when the header lists items
header acceptance time re-clocked with the frozen event_clock must still give a decision session strictly earlier than the 10-Q's
identity_checks.failure: An observed mismatch (another CIK, form, accession or item list) makes the event identity_failed, and a header acceptance that re-clocks to the 10-Q's session or later makes it header_not_prior; both stay in the sample as not stated in both bounds. A header that is fetched but lacks the accession, CIK, form or acceptance time, or whose acceptance cannot be clocked, leaves identity unverified: the release is still examined, and the event counts as not stated in the lower bound and by its components in the upper bound.

comparison_values.projection: Written to attempts/<id>/projection.json before any request: only the PROJECTED fields of probe.py (the components' values, their period endpoints, prior_fy_end, fiscal_year/fiscal_period, status and q_status) for the 150 sampled accessions. records.json is read with the decision-session audit's projection parser, which skips every other value without decoding it.
comparison_values.q_unavailable: A sampled event without a qualified Q keeps its S comparison; its Q components are reported as not_comparable and it leaves the Q denominator only in a separately reported row

matching.tables:
HTML tables parsed with the standard-library HTML parser (a
,

or

inside a cell separates words;
matching.plain_text: Cells are runs of text separated by two or more spaces (tabs expanded to 8) and keep their character offsets; from each header line a value takes the cell overlapping it most, else the nearest within 6 characters. A run of data lines is one table. Walking up from its first data line, a line with a cell starting right of that line's label is a header line, a line ending before its first value (a section label such as 'Revenues:') is skipped, and any other line ends the header. Inside a table a line with a cell right of the label ends the table. The other non-data lines since the previous data line are its context. Lines of only dashes, equals signs or underscores are skipped; non-table lines form paragraphs for the narrative rule.
matching.numbers: Commas removed; parentheses or a leading minus mean negative; a dash alone means zero; footnote markers ignored, including any <sup> text and a numbered marker such as '5.2(1)' after a value. Under a label naming only a loss ('net loss', not 'net income (loss)') or a use of cash ('cash used in', not 'provided by (used in)'), an unsigned amount is negative.
matching.scale: 1, 1e3, 1e6 or 1e9. A unit word in the value cell itself ('$5.2 million') fixes its scale. Otherwise the nearest unit phrase ('in thousands/millions/billions', 'thousands/millions/billions of dollars', '(000s)', '$000') fixes it, looking in order at the column header, the table-wide header cells, the caption and the preceding text; a bare scale word in prose (such as 'revenue was $2 billion') is not a unit phrase, and a level naming several units leaves every scale possible. Without a unit, an equal value at scale 1 counts normally, and an equal value only at a larger scale is scale_unverified: the multiplier was inferred from the 10-Q value, so it counts in the upper bound only. In prose the scale is the amount's own 'thousand', 'million' or 'billion' word, else 1.
matching.tolerance: half a unit of the displayed precision at that scale
matching.labels_note: Case-insensitive searches over the row's label cell text after whitespace is collapsed

periods.durations: three months, quarter or 12-14 weeks = 3; six months or 25-27 weeks = 6; nine months or 38-40 weeks = 9; twelve months, year or 51-53 weeks = 12; 'three and six months' names both durations; 'of fiscal year 2025' names the year a quarter belongs to and is not a twelve-month period
periods.end_dates: month-day-year; month-year, read as the last day of that month; or a year combined with a month-day phrase elsewhere in the same header, caption or context

required.current_ni: 3-month duration ending within 7 days of current_end
required.prior_ni: 3-month duration ending within 7 days of prior_end
required.q_current_cfo / q_current_ni: year-to-date duration (3, 6 or 9 months matching the 10-Q) ending within 7 days of q_current_end
required.q_prior_cfo / q_prior_ni: same duration ending within 7 days of q_prior_end
required.prior_fy_assets: an instant column dated within 7 days of prior_fy_end

periods.context: A column header with only a year takes its month-day from the table-wide context, and a dated header with no duration word takes its duration from it. Several durations or dates leave that part unparsed. A dated column with no duration or year-to-date word in its header or the context consulted is an instant.
periods.year_to_date: A 'year to date' header without a duration takes the 10-Q's year-to-date length: from q_current_start/q_current_end when Q is qualified, else three months times the fiscal quarter

matching.rule: A component is stated only when a table cell or narrative sentence, under a label that matches its pattern and none of the exclusions, equals the 10-Q value within the tolerance AND its column header or sentence parses to the required period. In a table, an equal value is dropped as a different period only when its parsed end date is more than 7 days from the required end or its parsed duration differs from the required one; any other equal value whose period is not verified (no date, an ambiguous duration, instant against duration) is period_unverified.
matching.evidence: Exhibit URL and SHA256, table and row index (or sentence and clause), label text, cell text, header text, parsed period and scale for every match; table and narrative matches under a contradicting period are kept with result different_period
matching.narrative: Text outside tables, each table row that is not a data row (prose laid out in tables), and each data row whose label cell runs on into its values (ending in 'was', 'were', 'is', 'are', 'of', 'totaled', 'amounted to', 'reached', 'to' or 'approximately'), each row joined into one text cell by cell, is split into sentences (at '.', ';', '!' or '?', optionally followed by up to two closing quotes or brackets, before a capital, lowercase letter, digit, quote or parenthesis, but never after an abbreviation such as 'Sept.', 'Inc.' or 'U.S.' or an initial, with or without closing marks) and each sentence into clauses at ';', 'compared with/to', 'versus', 'vs.' and ', and/while/whereas/up/down'. Each amount belongs to the nearest component label before it in its clause or, without one, to the last label of the nearest earlier clause of the same sentence; an amount whose owning label matches an exclusion (for example 'adjusted net income was $5.2 million' after 'net income was $4.0 million'), or with another measure named between it and its label (OTHER_METRIC in probe.py, or another component's label, for example 'and EBITDA was' or 'and cash flow from operations was'), does not count; nor does an amount introduced by a new subject after a comma, semicolon, 'and', 'while', 'whereas' or 'but' (or at the start of a clause whose label is carried) and before 'was', 'were', 'is', 'are', 'of', 'totaled', 'amounted to' or 'reached' (for example 'and income tax expense was'), unless the subject is a pronoun, a preposition or a period phrase such as 'first six months'; nor does an amount followed, before the next amount or 'and/while/whereas/but' and within 80 characters, by a non-GAAP or partial qualifier (adjusted, non-GAAP, pro forma, excluding, before (income) taxes, noncontrolling or minority interests, continuing or discontinued operations; QUALIFIER in probe.py), nor any amount in a clause with prospective wording (forecast, projected, projection, expect, anticipate, estimate, will/would/could/may/should be; PROSPECTIVE in probe.py), which is not a disclosure of the actual value. A label's exclusion check reads from 30 characters before it to the next amount, so 'net income attributable to noncontrolling interests' is excluded. Amounts may also be written '(5.2 million USD)'. Each narrative match records its clause, owning label, amount, scale, parsed period and fiscal-quarter phrases. An amount (a $, US$ or USD mark before it or USD after it, or another currency marked the same ways; an optional leading minus or parenthesis; an optional 'thousand', 'million' or 'billion' word setting the scale) equal to the 10-Q value is stated when a period phrase in the same clause parses to the required period ('three months ended June 30, 2024', 'year to date') or names the 10-Q's fiscal quarter and year ('second quarter of fiscal 2024', 'Q2 FY2024', 'FY24 Q2', 'fiscal 2024 second quarter'; one year earlier for prior-year values) with no date or duration in the clause contradicting the requirement. A clause whose dated period or fiscal-quarter phrase contradicts the requirement does not count; a clause with several amounts and several periods (several dates, fiscal quarters, distinct years as in 'June 30, 2025 and 2024 ... respectively', or durations as in 'second quarter and first six months') cannot be paired and is period_unverified, as is a clause naming several durations, several distinct fiscal quarters (counting those followed by their own end date), several distinct dates, or no period phrase; a fiscal-quarter phrase followed by 'ended <date>' describes one period.
matching.currency: A leading or trailing $, US$ or USD is removed and recorded in the evidence. An equal amount marked with any other currency (any letter-prefixed dollar other than US$, such as C$, CA$, A$ or HK$; CAD, EUR, GBP or AUD; the euro or pound sign) is recorded as currency_mismatch: it is not the USD 10-Q component and counts as not stated in both bounds. A unit phrase naming another currency in the table caption or context (table-wide; a column header's currency applies only to its own column) (for example '(in millions of Canadian dollars)', '(in millions of Australian dollars)', '(AUD in millions)', '(Canadian dollars in millions)' or 'C$ in thousands') makes the table's values currency_mismatch; a passing mention of a currency in prose does not.
matching.label_exclusions: adjusted|non-?gaap|pro forma|\bcore\b|excluding|\bbefore\b|per (basic |diluted )?(common )?share|margin|non-?controlling|minority|continuing|discontinued (case-insensitive; for narrative sentences it is checked from 30 characters before to 25 after the label)
matching.specification: probe.py and test_probe.py are bound by SHA256 in freeze.json and define these rules exactly; this prose summarises them

classification: scale_unverified (equal only at a scale inferred without a unit phrase)
currency_mismatch (an equal amount in another currency)
exhibit_unavailable (unsupported_format, image_dependent, exhibit_overflow, release_unidentified or fetch failure)

statistics.per_component: For each component, the share of comparable events stated, with the same lower and upper bounds as the signals and Wilson 95% intervals for both
statistics.per_signal: share with every S_flow component stated, and with every Q_flow component stated; assets reported separately
statistics.bounds: A signal is lower-bound stated when every component in it is stated and the event is neither release_ambiguous nor identity_unverified. It is upper-bound stated when every component is stated, period_unverified, scale_unverified or exhibit_unavailable (for a release_ambiguous event the candidates are matched jointly, so a component found in none of them stays not stated). currency_mismatch, label_only, not_found, identity_failed and header_not_prior are not stated in both bounds.

interpretation.per_signal: For S_flow and Q_flow separately: release_complete_common if the Wilson lower limit of the lower-bound share is at least 0.7; release_complete_rare if the Wilson upper limit of the upper-bound share is below 0.3; otherwise inconclusive
interpretation.common: Justifies only a separately declared full-population extraction of that signal's components from the releases
interpretation.never: No verdict backdates a 10-Q value, changes a completed result, promotes a strategy or implies profitability

verification: Before freezing: offline synthetic tests (test_probe.py) for every rule and for the fetch lifecycle with a fake opener. After the run: probe.py --reanalyze recomputes every classification from the saved bytes and must reproduce events.json, summary.json and spot-check.json exactly, and each of those files must still have the SHA256 recorded in attempt.json; its 'reproduced' value is true, and its exit status 0, only when all of these hold. spot-check.json lists the 20 sampled events with the smallest SHA256 of 'exhibit-content20261002|spot|' + 10-Q accession, a membership fixed before and independent of any classification, with their evidence for an owner reading of the original documents; disagreements are reported with the results. This replaces the draft's separately written checker.

lifecycle.fetch: The frozen capture's Cache class, executed from its verified bytes (SHA256 962bccbf…), under attempts/<id>/source/: a request_started row is fsynced to requests.jsonl before each request; each URL's outcome is saved once under resources/; a URL with a saved outcome is never requested again; a started URL without an outcome may be requested once more; 403/429 or an oversize response writes STOP.json and halts. A URL that reaches its per-URL attempt ceiling, the lifetime ceiling or the total raw-byte ceiling without an outcome gets STOP.json and then a terminal failure record (never requested again; the stop is written first so a crash between them still needs the review), so after the owner's acknowledgement its event is unavailable rather than halting every resume; once a lifetime or byte stop is acknowledged, later unfetched URLs fail the same way without another stop. Before the cache opens, raw files whose bytes no longer match their SHA256 name (a crash during the cache's direct write) are moved to source/partial and listed in attempt.json, and an incomplete last line of requests.jsonl (a crash during the cache's append; the cache sends a request only after its request_started line is written, so a cut line was never a sent request) is moved to source/partial with its size and SHA256 recorded in attempt.json; a complete journal line that does not parse stops the run for review.
lifecycle.transport: A transport failure (no HTTP status) writes STOP.json and halts the attempt, so a network outage cannot silently fail every event. A saved transport failure whose URL is not in an acknowledged STOP record halts again on resume, so a crash between saving the failure and writing STOP.json cannot skip the owner's review.
locks: exclusive study lock probe.lock.sqlite, held for the whole run
exclusive transaction on the shared .qualification/earnings-quality20260928/sec-source.lock.sqlite, so no other SEC source worker runs at the same time
a held lock refuses the start; a free study lock means no live worker of this study exists

under both locks and before any attempt is created or resumed, the running processes are listed (PowerShell Get-CimInstance on Windows, ps elsewhere); any Python process other than this one and its ancestors whose command line runs something under .qualification refuses the start, because older SEC capture workers hold only their own lock. If the processes cannot be listed the start is refused.
lifecycle.attempt: One attempt per frozen definition under attempts/<uuid>/, with attempt.json (definition and code SHA256s, runtime, status) replaced atomically. A new attempt's folder appears only by renaming a dot-named staging folder that already holds its attempt.json, so a crash before that rename leaves no attempt (the staging folder made no request; preflight lists it). Existing attempts are checked under the study lock: a completed or failed attempt refuses any new run; a new attempt needs a declared amendment.
lifecycle.resume: probe.py --resume ID continues a running or halted attempt after the same checks, only when the attempt's recorded code SHA256s equal the active freeze's; the saved sample must equal the recomputed one, a projection interrupted before it was written is completed before any request, a projection written but not yet recorded must equal a fresh projection of the verified records.json before it is bound by its SHA256, and a recorded projection must still match. attempt.json keeps the runtime the attempt began with and records each resume's runtime beside it. Before a resume's first request the probe waits until the declared interval has passed since the last journaled request. A halted attempt resumes only with --acknowledge-stop, which keeps the STOP record renamed beside it. --reanalyze accepts only a complete attempt of the frozen definition, code and inputs, and every saved payload it reads, an error response's included, must still match its recorded size and SHA256; a completed attempt records in attempt.json the SHA256 of every file under source/ except the content-addressed raw payloads (the request journal, resource records, stops and quarantined parts), and --reanalyze reports reproduced only when they are unchanged; it rechecks the SHA256 of the timing events and calendar it reads (records.json is not read; the projection's SHA256 recorded in attempt.json is checked instead).

documents.supported: HTML (by .htm/.html name or an <html>/<table> sniff) and plain text (.txt)
documents.unsupported: PDF (%PDF), images and any other binary are exhibit_unavailable (unsupported_format)
documents.image_dependent: Per component, not per document. A component that is not stated, period_unverified or scale_unverified (including one that is only currency_mismatch) is exhibit_unavailable (image_dependent) when the document has an whose alt text, file name (URL-decoded, with '_', '-', '+' and '.' read as spaces) or the 300 characters of text before it in source order (in or out of tables) name the statement that would hold it (a statement of income, operations or earnings; a statement of cash flows; a balance sheet or statement of financial condition or position), even when the label appears elsewhere in the document. A logo, chart or any other image does not change label_only or not_found.
documents.press_release: Press-release candidates are fetched EX-99 documents whose index description, or whose first 3,000 characters of text in source order, match (press|news|earnings) release case-insensitively. Exactly one candidate is the release. With none, the single EX-99.1 is used and flagged release_by_type; with no single EX-99.1 the event is release_unidentified (unavailable). With several, all candidates are matched jointly and the event is flagged release_ambiguous.
documents.secondary: Availability in any fetched EX-99 document is reported as a separate, non-verdict readout, for every event whose identity checks pass and whose identity is verified (identity_unverified events are excluded), including release_unidentified events
documents.combination: When several documents are matched jointly (release_ambiguous candidates, or any EX-99 document for the secondary readout), the component takes the first of stated, period_unverified, scale_unverified, exhibit_unavailable, currency_mismatch, label_only, not_found found in any of them, so a candidate that may hold the value keeps it possible.

every bound code and input SHA256

owner_decisions.2026-10-02: Accept the draft defaults: the 1,166-event decision-session single_prior frame, a 150-event sample, thresholds 0.7 and 0.3, and the frozen capture's user agent. Run on the owner's workstation, which also performs the records.json projection.
